title: Rigveda 9.59: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.59: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.59 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 688r-688v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.59.1-3 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 688r
translation.original_text:
1pava̍sva go̱jid a̍śva̱jid vi̍śva̱jit so̍ma raṇya̱jit | pra̱jāva̱d ratna̱m ā bha̍ra ||
2pava̍svā̱dbhyo adā̍bhya̱ḥ pava̱svauṣa̍dhībhyaḥ | pava̍sva dhi̱ṣaṇā̍bhyaḥ ||
3tvaṁ so̍ma̱ pava̍māno̱ viśvā̍ni duri̱tā ta̍ra | ka̱viḥ sī̍da̱ ni ba̱rhiṣi̍ ||
translation.text:
1FLOW onward, Soma, winning kine, and steeds, and all that gives delight: Bring hither wealth with progeny.
2Flow onward from the waters, flow, inviolable, from the plants: Flow onward from the pressing-boards.
3Soma, as Pavamâna, pass over all trouble and distress: Sit on the sacred grass, a Sage.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 688r (numbered 5r by the scribe) (OPenn image 688, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.57.2 ‹cakṣāṇaḥ arṣati hariḥ tuñjānaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 688v (numbered 5v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.59.4 ‹asi›. Verses 9.59.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pavasva | go-jit | aśva-jit | viśva-jit | soma | raṇya-jit | prajāvat | ratnam | ā | bhara
2pavasva | at-bhyaḥ | adābhyaḥ | pavasva | oṣadhībhyaḥ | pavasva | dhiṣaṇābhyaḥ
3tvam | soma | pavamānaḥ | viśvāni | duḥ-itā | tara | kaviḥ | sīda | ni | barhiṣi

translation.original_ref: RV 9.59.4 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 688v
translation.original_text: <sup>4</sup>pava̍māna̱ sva̍r vido̱ jāya̍māno 'bhavo ma̱hān | indo̱ viśvā̍m̐ a̱bhīd a̍si ||
translation.text: <sup>4</sup>Thou, Pavamâna, foundest light; thou at thy birth becamest great: O Indu, thou art over all.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 688v (numbered 5v by the scribe) (OPenn image 689, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.59.4 ‹asi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 689r (numbered 6r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.61.6 ‹ā bhara rayim vīra-vatīm›. Verse 9.59.4 ends on this page; 9.59.4 begins on fol. 688r (numbered 5r by the scribe).
translation.edition_text: <sup>4</sup>pavamāna | svaḥ | vidaḥ | jāyamānaḥ | abhavaḥ | mahān | indo iti | viśvān | abhi | it | asi
